_readme: Product marketing framework for the Tungsten Smart-Heat® Gas family (owner, 19 Nov 2026; schema v2 for range frameworks). One framework, two forms: the mounted Tungsten Smart-Heat® Gas (wall, ceiling or pole, two sizes, natural gas or propane) and the wheeled Tungsten Smart-Heat® Freestanding gas tower (sold for years as Tungsten Portable; the site, manuals and image files still use that name). Matrix 1: what matters to each buyer (w 3 matters most, 2 matters, 1 nice to have) and the claim that lands. Matrix 2: mounted against freestanding, so sales know which to propose. Matrix 3: against the closest US gas competitors, mounted and freestanding (factual, sourced, needs_approval Specification and compliance). Built-in Tungsten Gas BTU stays unpublished until the Product team confirms it (CLAUDE.md hard rule 3); legacy series numbers are never used. Bromic facts come from data/product-facts.json; where a Bromic document read on 19 Nov 2026 (cut sheets, US manuals) adds a fact not yet in product-facts, it is cited and carries a [[VERIFY]]. Competitor facts are from the makers' own pages and spec sheets where they could be read; retailer-hosted copies of maker spec sheets are cited as such.

m2_label.intro: Which Tungsten Gas to propose: the mounted heater where there is a roof, a beam and a gas line; the tower where the space is open, changes nightly or has no fixing point.

m2.s1: Electronic ignition with flame monitoring (the ignition control shuts the gas within 1 s of a running flame failure, US manual). Mounted at least 96 in above the floor; top clearance 3 ft, or 14 in with the heat deflector. ETL and cETL listing 4009079.
m2.s2: Flame failure device and anti-tilt switch (US manual). 3 ft clearance to the sides and above (US manual); minimum floor clearance 121 in (cut sheet) [[VERIFY: what the 121 in figure measures — Product team]]. Intertek listing 4009079 shown for the propane model.
m2.so_what: Mounted keeps the heat out of reach; the tower keeps itself safe when it is bumped or tipped. Both shut the gas when the flame goes out.

m2.s1: Two sizes: up to 160 ft² and up to 215 ft² (bromic.com; in ideal conditions per the cut sheet). [[VERIFY: built-in output by model; bromic.com and the US manual publish figures that conflict with the 2021 Planning Guide, so no built-in BTU is used until confirmed — Product team]]
m2.s2: 38,000 BTU, about 215 ft² (Lookbook 2026). [[VERIFY: 38,000 BTU (Lookbook 2026) against 38,500 BTU (bromic.com, cut sheet and US manual) — Product team]]
m2.so_what: Same reach as the larger mounted heater from a tower that moves; the smaller mounted size suits tighter bays.

m2.s1: Wall bracket (one included per heater), ceiling poles 9.69 to 41.18 in for flat or pitched ceilings (poles hang vertical), pivot arm ±25°, optional heat deflector.
m2.s2: Built-in wheels, no fixing. Propane model is self-contained; natural gas model connects through a 10 ft quick-connect line.
m2.so_what: Propose mounted for fixed seating under a roof; the tower for open terraces, lawns, pool decks and layouts that change.

m2.s1: IPX4 (cut sheet). Must be protected from rain and installed under a protective cover (US manual). Wind: [[VERIFY: mounted wind rating; bromic.com says up to 8 mph, the US manual V2.3 says designed to function in winds up to 10 mph — Product team]] Stainless steel with a high-temperature coating.
m2.s2: IPX4 (cut sheet), 304 stainless steel, wind up to 8 mph (bromic.com). Protective head cover sold separately ($108).
m2.so_what: The tower can stand in the open; the mounted heater belongs under a roof, pergola cover or awning.

m2.s1: Natural gas or propane, one factory SKU per gas. 1/2 in NPT female inlet; inlet 6 to 14 in W.C. (natural gas) or 11 to 14 in W.C. (propane).
m2.s2: Propane from a 20 lb cylinder in the base, or natural gas through the 10 ft quick-connect line; same pressure ranges.
m2.so_what: Every Tungsten Gas model comes in both gases, so the site's supply never rules one out.

m2.s1: No switch on the heater: it is switched by its power supply, from an Affinity Smart-Heat® On/Off Controller (Bromic app, zones, schedules, timers, smart-home and BMS integration) or a manual wall switch. On/off only, no dimming. [[VERIFY: Affinity On/Off spec table lists only electric heaters while its intro and FAQ add gas (up to 10 gas heaters a channel); confirm gas compatibility and capacity — Product team]]
m2.s2: At the heater: push-button spark ignition (one AAA battery), gas knob. Propane adjusts from high to low; natural gas runs on high only. No app control.
m2.so_what: Mounted is the smart, zoned choice; the tower is the simple one. Offer Affinity controls with every mounted heater.

m2.s1: Compact honeycomb face in matte black, about 19.3 in or 25.4 in wide (US manual drawing).
m2.s2: Sculpted curved column in matte black, about 85 in tall (2,160 mm, US manual).
m2.so_what: Mounted all but disappears into the structure; the tower is a piece of furniture people notice.

m2.s1: Pivot arm turns ±25° to each side; angle down from the wall or ceiling.
m2.s2: Adjustable tilting head with a high tilt position, set before lighting (US manual).
m2.so_what: Both aim the heat at people; the tower also aims it from wherever it is parked.

m2.s1: Cut sheet, US manual, wiring diagram, clearance drawings, complimentary design service.
m2.s2: Cut sheet, US manual, clearance and heat coverage drawings, complimentary design service.
m2.so_what: Either way, a free design plan settles how many and where.

m2.s1: Licensed gas fitter and electrician: fixed gas pipe, 110 V supply under 2 A, bracket or pole. [[VERIFY: whether a cord-and-plug connection is permitted in the US or hard-wiring is required — Product team]]
m2.s2: Assembles from two boxes, then rolls into place. Propane: fit a cylinder. Natural gas: a fitter provides the quick-connect point.
m2.so_what: The tower can be warming guests the day it arrives; mounted is a planned install.

m2.s1: Group heaters on controller channels and zones; up to 10 gas heaters a channel. [[VERIFY: Affinity On/Off spec table lists only electric heaters while its intro and FAQ add gas (up to 10 gas heaters a channel); confirm gas compatibility and capacity — Product team]]
m2.s2: One heater, one table group; move towers between areas as the evening changes.
m2.so_what: Mix them: mounted zones under the roof, towers at the open edge.

m2.s1: 2 years, excluding maintenance items such as hoses and igniters (bromic.com warranty page).
m2.s2: 1 year (bromic.com warranty page; shown for the propane model).
m2.so_what: Mounted carries the longer cover; say so when a client weighs the two.

m3.intro: Against the closest US gas competitors: Sunpak and Schwank for mounted heaters, Sunglo, Schwank's parasol and AZ Patio's glass-tube towers for freestanding. Heatstrip (AU) is noted for the Australian team but not benchmarked here.

competitors.name: Sunpak S34 TSH (mounted)
competitors.owner: Infrared Dynamics, Inc. (Yorba Linda, California); sold through AEI Corporation
competitors.why_closest: The best-known mounted ceramic infrared gas patio heater in US residential and restaurant work: wall or ceiling, natural gas or propane, 25,000 to 34,000 BTU, the heater a dealer most often quotes against Tungsten Gas.

competitors.name: Schwank supremeSchwank (mounted) and parasolSchwank (freestanding)
competitors.owner: Schwank Group (US base Waynesboro, Georgia; Canada Mississauga)
competitors.why_closest: The commercial gas heating brand restaurants and specifiers know, with a mounted ceramic heater in 316 marine-grade stainless steel and a wheeled propane parasol: the one rival that covers both Tungsten Gas forms.

competitors.name: Sunglo A242 (freestanding)
competitors.owner: Infrared Dynamics, Inc.; sold through AEI Corporation
competitors.why_closest: The long-standing commercial freestanding patio heater (50,000 BTU, natural gas or propane, CSA design certified): the restaurant-grade tower a Tungsten Freestanding replaces.

competitors.name: AZ Patio Heaters 55K glass-tube tower (freestanding)
competitors.owner: AZ Patio Heaters (products sold under the Hiland name; parent not stated on its site)
competitors.why_closest: The design-led flame tower homeowners and casual venues buy at a fraction of the price: wheels, propane, anti-tilt device, a visible flame. Sets the price anchor the freestanding tower is judged against.

rows.bromic: Freestanding: flame failure device and anti-tilt switch (US manual). Mounted: electronic ignition with flame monitoring and lockout (US manual). ETL and cETL listing 4009079. Mounted at least 96 in above the floor.

vs.sunpak: Direct spark ignition with auto re-light and flame sensor; "100% shutoff for safety"; CSA design certified to ANSI Z83.19 (Infrared Dynamics).
vs.schwank: supremeSchwank "UL Certified" (schwankgroup.com), 8 ft minimum mounting height. parasolSchwank tech specs list push-button battery spark; no tip-over device is listed [[VERIFY: tilt switch on parasolSchwank — Specification and compliance]].
vs.sunglo: "100% Safety Shutoff" with pilot and thermocouple; CSA design certified to ANSI Z83.19; optional tie-down kit for public spaces. A tip-over switch is claimed only in a retailer Q&A [[VERIFY — Specification and compliance]].

battlecard.objection: A Sunpak costs less and I know it.
battlecard.answer: Tungsten Gas comes with its wall bracket and runs on 110 V, so there is no 24 VAC transformer to add, its head is about half the length of a 4 ft bar, and with Affinity controls the whole patio switches from the app. [[VERIFY: Sunpak street price — Sales operations]]

battlecard.objection: Schwank is 316 stainless and has a 3-year warranty.
battlecard.answer: Both true. Tungsten Gas carries 2 years on mounted heaters and is built for covered spaces; where salt air is the brief, talk to our team about the right Bromic heater for the coast. Our wins are the compact head, app control and a freestanding tower in the same family.

battlecard.objection: Why pay over $2,000 for a tower when a glass-tube heater is $470?
battlecard.answer: The Tungsten tower aims its warmth at the table with a tilting head, has a flame failure device and an anti-tilt switch, is 304 stainless, and comes in natural gas as well as propane.

battlecard.objection: Mushroom heaters have worked on our patio for years.
battlecard.answer: They radiate down and around the pole. The Tungsten tower tilts its head to put the heat on the seats, and our free design plan shows how many you need.

battlecard.objection: Can I dim a gas heater?
battlecard.answer: Mounted Tungsten Gas is on or off, switched by Affinity controls with schedules and timers; the propane tower adjusts from high to low at the knob. For dimmable warmth under a roof, look at Tungsten Smart-Heat® Electric.

battlecard.objection: What about wind on an open terrace?
battlecard.answer: Radiant heat warms people, so it holds up better than heaters that warm the air; place towers out of the strongest wind and let the design team plan the layout. [[VERIFY: published wind rating before quoting a figure — Product team]]
